text:
ria: Kicking off kubeadm bootstrap for ap-ne3 GPU cluster. Target topology: 3 control-plane nodes (kubeadm stacked), 6 GPU worker nodes (A100-ish), Cilium as CNI, MTU 1500 (SG/network team asked for 1500 due to on-prem transit), Pod CIDR 10.40.0.0/16, Service CIDR 10.96.0.0/12. Posting preflight + current questions.

sam: Quick Q — are we doing encryption at transit for etcd? We should enable TLS and KMS integration for control-plane certs.

ria: Yes — etcd TLS on by default, certs from Vault. KMS for kubelet cert rotation planned. I'll add the KMS ARN to the bootstrap-config.

mike: On the worker side, reminder: NVIDIA drivers must install as a daemonset; use nvidia-container-toolkit now, not nvidia-docker2. Last time we had a node stuck in NotReady because driver DS timed out.

anna: Also we'll need node-feature-discovery and device-plugin labels for scheduling. Plan to add labels: "gpu=true", "gpu.family=A100" and taint node.k8s.io/gpu:NoSchedule. We'll use tolerations on inference deployments.

ria: Preflight checklist I'm running through:
- VPC routes verified
- Subnet MTU set to 1500 (confirmed with net team)
- SSH bastion ready for node debugging
- kubeadm config.yaml uploaded to S3: includes apiEndpoint, podSubnet, serviceSubnet, controlPlaneEndpoint
- Calico vs Cilium: choosing Cilium for eBPF perf and BPF masquerade
- KMS keys present, audit logging enabled

sam: If Cilium, watch MTU — we saw fragmentation with 1500 -> make sure cilium-agent uses host MTU or configure tunnel-mtu accordingly.

ria: Good call. I'll set tunnel: disabled and use ENI routing mode where possible to avoid encapsulation.

mike: Noted a potential kube-proxy compatibility issue if we switch to cilium-mode=none. We should disable kube-proxy after cilium is stable. Plan: deploy cilium in kube-proxy-replacement=partial first, validate connectivity, then full.

ria: Boot commands for control-plane nodes (example):
```bash
kubeadm init --config=/etc/kubeadm/config.yaml --upload-certs
mkdir -p /etc/kubernetes/pki/some-override
```
Will run with control-plane taints and join tokens rotated via vault.

anna: GPU node userdata snippet to install drivers (debian-based):
```bash
# install deps
apt update && apt install -y dkms build-essential
# install nvidia driver via package repo
apt install -y nvidia-driver-525
# install nvidia-container-toolkit
curl -s -L https://nvidia.github.io/nvidia-docker/gpgkey | apt-key add -
# follow nvidia steps to configure repo && apt install nvidia-container-toolkit
systemctl restart docker
```
Expect this to add ~3-5 mins to node join time.

mike: If driver DS keeps failing, check dmesg for module ABI mismatch. Last time we had kernel version drift on a few images. Suggest pinning AMI/kernel image family for GPU pool.

ria: Agree — locking to gpu-runtime-2026-02-01 image. I'll add that to the nodepool config and to the handoff doc.

sam: Autoscaler/cost note: We prefer MixedInstanceTypes with spot fallback for dev pools, but for production inference use on-demand reserved. Make sure cluster-autoscaler has GPU resource-awareness and labels to avoid evicting critical pods.

anna: Also set PodTopologySpread for GPU jobs to avoid binpacking on a single AZ; that'll help reliability.

ops-bot: deploy-bot reports: kubeadm config validated, no obvious YAML schema errors.

ria: Current blocker: cilium-agent daemonset shows 2/6 pods in CrashLoopBackOff on worker nodes with error "failed to allocate BPF map" — suspect low rlimit or kernel config. Can someone grab sysctl and dmesg from a failing node?

mike: I'll SSH into node-5 now via bastion. Quick checks I run:
- sysctl net.core.rmem_max net.core.wmem_max
- iptables -L (should be minimal)
- dmesg | grep cilium

mike: dmesg shows: "cilium: bpf syscall: Invalid argument" and "BPF creation failed: errno 22". sysctl net.core.rmem_max=212992 reported. I'll raise rlimits and try restart cilium pod.

ria: Thanks — after rlimit bump, restart cilium-daemonset and check logs: `kubectl -n kube-system logs ds/cilium`

mike: After bump + restart, cilium-agent stable on that node. Suggest we add the sysctl/limits to userdata so new nodes don't break.

anna: For handoff to oncall: I'll draft minimal runbook steps:
1) Verify control-plane health: `kubectl get cs && kubectl get nodes`
2) Check GPU plugin DS: `kubectl -n kube-system get ds nvidia-driver-installer`
3) Check cilium status: `cilium status` and `kubectl -n kube-system logs ds/cilium`
4) Verify example inference deployment scheduling on GPU with tolerations/limits
5) Validate cross-AZ traffic and service e2e latency (simple curl against model service)

ria: I'll update the cluster handoff doc in Confluence and attach AMI, kubeadm-config, and nodepool specs.

deploy-bot: cluster bootstrap job started: job-id=cb-1990012345, trackers sent to #eng-oncall.

sam: Anything else on networking? Make sure NAT gateway costs are projected: 6 GPU nodes outbound egress to S3 for model fetch could be nontrivial. ops-finance flagged estimated $120/mo for dev clusters; production will be higher.

ria: Noted — will add a cost estimate section to the handoff. For now, proceeding with the rlimit + AMI pin + cilium host MTU config. Planning to run smoke tests after join.

mike: I'll stay on watch for the next hour to catch node join flaps. Ping me if any nodes show NotReady.

ria: Thanks all — will post status updates here. :thumbsup:
